title: Limiting terms: だけ, しか, ばかり, のみ
summary: Four ways to say "only", each with its own mood: だけ is neutral, しか feels too little, ばかり feels a lot, のみ is formal.

blocks.text: All four mean "only" in English, which is why they confuse people. In Japanese each one has a character.
**だけ** is a noun meaning "limit". It adds no feeling: just where something stops.

blocks.en: I have a thousand yen, no more (a plain fact).

blocks.text: Two common phrases: **できるだけ** (to the limit of what is possible: as much as I can) and **だけあって** (precisely because of that limit).

blocks.jp: できるだけ勉強します。
blocks.en: I will study as much as I can.

blocks.jp: 留学しただけあって、英語がうまい。
blocks.en: Precisely because she studied abroad, her English is good.

blocks.jp: 安いだけあって、すぐに壊れてしまった。
blocks.en: Precisely because it was cheap, it broke right away.

blocks.text: The textbook gloss "no wonder" only fits the good result. The second sentence shows the real meaning: the result matches the cause, good or bad.
**しか** means "more than" and is used with a **negative** ending, so the sentence says "not more than". It feels like "too little".

blocks.jp: 千円しか持っていない。
blocks.en: I have only a thousand yen (that is not much).
There is nothing to do but run.

blocks.text: ばかり: so much of one thing
**ばかり** exaggerates the other way: "just that", with a feel of abundance (lesson 27).

blocks.jp: この店はパンばかり売っている。
blocks.en: This shop sells nothing but bread (so much bread).

blocks.text: **のみ** means the same as だけ but belongs to signs, rules and writing. Recognize it; you will rarely say it.

blocks.jp: 会員のみ入場できます。

blocks.text: The same shop and the same bread, with four different feelings.

rows: Only bread; that is too little
Only bread; so much of it

items: **しか + negative**: not more than; feels scarce.

questions.prompt: ケーキを一つだけ食べた。
questions.note: だけ is a plain limit.

questions.prompt: ケーキを一つしか食べなかった。
questions.note: しか + negative: scarcity.
questions.en: I ate only one cake (that was too few).

questions.prompt: 今日は朝ごはんを少し＿＿食べなかった。
questions.note: しか needs a negative ending.
questions.en: I ate only a little breakfast today.

questions.prompt: 弟はゲーム＿＿している。勉強はしない。
questions.note: ばかり: nothing but one thing, in abundance.
questions.en: My little brother does nothing but play games. He does not study.

questions.instruction: Which sentence feels like "there were too few students"?
options: 学生が三人しか来なかった。
questions.note: しか + negative: scarcity.
しか needs a negative ending.

questions.instruction: Which sentence sounds the most formal, like a sign?
questions.note: のみ is a written, formal だけ.

questions.instruction: What does できるだけ mean?
questions.prompt: できるだけ早く返事をください。
questions.note: To the limit of what is possible.
questions.en: Please reply as soon as possible.

questions.instruction: What does だけあって say?
questions.prompt: 毎日練習しているだけあって、ピアノが上手だ。
options: Although he practices, he is bad
Precisely because of the cause, the result follows
Practice is the only thing he does
questions.note: だけあって: precisely because of that.
questions.en: Precisely because he practices every day, he is good at the piano.

questions.prompt: 田中さんは十年住んだ＿＿、道をよく知っている。
questions.note: A result that fits its cause.
questions.en: Precisely because he lived there for ten years, Mr. Tanaka knows the streets well.

questions.instruction: What feeling does ばかり give?
questions.prompt: 彼は肉ばかり食べている。
questions.note: ばかり: a feeling of abundance.

questions.prompt: しか can be followed by a positive verb ending.
questions.note: しか always goes with a negative.

questions.prompt: もう少し待つしかない。
options: There is nothing to do but wait a little longer
questions.note: Verb + しかない: no choice but to.
questions.en: There is nothing to do but wait a little longer.

questions.instruction: What does だけ mean at its root?
questions.note: だけ is a noun meaning "limit".
Amount + だけ: a plain limit.

questions.prompt: Yesterday I could sleep only two hours.
questions.note: しか + negative.
questions.en: Yesterday I could sleep only two hours.

questions.prompt: My older sister reads nothing but manga.
questions.note: ばかり: just that, in abundance.
questions.en: My older sister reads nothing but manga.

questions.prompt: There is nothing to do but go by bus.
questions.note: Verb + しかない.
questions.en: There is nothing to do but go by bus.

questions.instruction: Tap the part that means "too little"
questions.note: しか + negative: scarcity.
questions.en: This month I could rest only one day.

questions.instruction: Tap the part that shows abundance
questions.note: ばかり: so much of one thing.
questions.en: This child eats nothing but sweets.

questions.instruction: Tap the part that is a neutral limit
questions.note: だけ: just where it stops.
questions.en: Only three people can enter here.

questions.instruction: What does だけあって say here?
questions.prompt: 安いだけあって、すぐ壊れた。
options: Although it was cheap, it did not break
Precisely because it was cheap, it broke
It was cheap, so I bought it
questions.note: だけあって matches result to cause, even a bad result.
questions.en: Precisely because it was cheap, it broke soon.
